raw_response:
I've been working this land for 40 years. I know every corner of it. My wheat and maize rotation on 8 mu is what keeps my family fed and pays for basics. The other 6 mu I put into cotton — I've grown it my whole life, I know when it's thirsty, I know when the bollworm is coming.

My sons and daughters tell me to drop the cotton because picking is hard at my age and they're not around to help. But I know cotton. The price was decent last year and I'll manage. I'll hire a day laborer or two for harvest if I have to.

For wheat, I plant it every autumn after the maize comes off. I use the improved seed from the township seed shop — not the old varieties, those don't yield as well. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and then urea at jointing. I irrigate before winter sets in, again at jointing, and at heading. That's three times, maybe four if it's dry at grain fill. I spray once for weeds in spring and once for aphids.

For maize, I direct-seed it right after wheat harvest in June — no time to plow, and it works fine. I use hybrid seed,郑单 type, same as my neighbors. I top-dress nitrogen twice. I water at jointing and at silking.

For cotton, I plow the 6 mu in early spring and transplant seedlings in late April. Cotton takes more work — more spraying, more watering. I'll spray five or six times over the season for bollworm and aphids. I water four times: at budding, first flower, boll setting, and if August is dry.

I don't change much from year to year. What worked before, I keep doing.
